newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia expresses concern over PNG crisis.
newsitem.headline: Australia expresses concern over PNG crisis.

text.p: Australia said on Monday it opposed any unconstitutional move against the government of Papua New Guinea after the country's army chief turned against plans to use mercenaries on Bougainville island.
"The government is following the situation very closely and with great concern," a spokesman for Australian Prime Minister John Howard told Reuters.

"The government opposes any unconstitutional moves against the PNG government. The government calls on the PNG government and parliament to resolve the matter as soon as possible, peacefully, and in accordance with the constitution."
Brigadier General Jerry Singirok, PNG defence force commander, on Monday announced his opposition to a government plan to use mercenaries to end a nine-year secessionist revolt on Bougainville.

He also ordered the detention of 40 African mercenaries in the country training troops for a mission to Bougainville and gave Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan and two other ministers 48 hours to quit or be forced to do so.
Singirok denied, however, that he was staging a coup.
Australia, backed by the United States and New Zealand, has vigorously opposed Chan's plans to use mercenaries to end the Bougainville war, which has killed thousands of people.
"(This) is this sort of destabilisation that we feared the introduction of such mercenaries into PNG and the region might cause," Howard's spokesman said.
"The government has not been asked to intervene militarily and the situation does not require that," he said.
